key_insight: For nonlinear PDEs, a first-order least-squares residual can reliably measure solution error in the PDE-compliant norm under stability and regularity conditions.
engineering_relevance: This provides a principled training loss and inference-time error indicator for neural PDE surrogates without requiring labeled solutions for residual-based training.
method: Prove local residual–error equivalence using linearized stability and Lipschitz continuity of the residual derivative.
Verify conditions for monotone reaction, nonlinear diffusion, and compressible Neo-Hookean hyperelasticity.
Train a finite-element reduced-basis neural operator using library-assembled losses and symbolic gradients; use solution snapshots only to build the basis.
evidence_signal: Numerical tests show that the square root of loss excess tracks error with factors comparable to the linear case, while the operator outperforms grid-based baselines in the PDE-compliant norm.
watch_item: Guarantees depend on equation-specific stability and regularity, may hold only near a solution branch, and can require control in a stronger norm.
paper_title: Variationally correct physics-informed operator learning for nonlinear partial differential equations
